subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: A collection of generic low-level runtime helpers in the 0x0051F890-0x005668EC range: 20 unconditional tail-jump forwarding thunks, 14 empty no-op placeholder stubs, fixed-point arithmetic primitives, 16-bit/32-bit pixel fill and blit routines, string/buffer scan helpers, plus a CRC-style checksum, a min-heap sift-down, a bit-reversal helper, an x87 float power helper, and several suspect/artifact stubs. No packet evidence ties these functions to a common owning class; the groupings below are behavioral proposals only.

summary: This packet contains 54 generic runtime functions. The dominant patterns are (1) bare JUMPOUT forwarding thunks whose real bodies live at targets outside the packet, and (2) empty nullsub placeholders. The remaining functions are small self-contained helpers: 16.16 fixed-point multiply/divide and float-to-int conversion, 16-bit and 32-bit pixel fill/blit routines, a relative-offset string copy, an n-th backslash scanner, a CRC-style checksum, a min-heap sift-down, a bit-reversal helper, and an x87 power helper. Three functions carry decompiler 'positive sp value' warnings and are treated as unreliable (0x00554E04, 0x005631C4, 0x0056498E); two others are probable inline-asm decompiler artifacts (0x0055685A, and the MK_FP bare-return stubs 0x0052D294/0x0052D2A4). Ownership of every function is unknown from the packet; class assignments are GUESS-level behavioral groupings, and each jump thunk's target is unresolved.

16.16 fixed-point multiply with rounding: signed 64-bit product, add 0x8000 (half of 2^16), shift right 16, return the 32-bit result.

Pixel blit copying a rectangular region from a 16-bit source buffer to a 32-bit destination buffer, expanding each 16-bit pixel into a 32-bit word and skipping pixels equal to the reference color a11 (color-key); address arithmetic built from flat base/stride/count parameters.

16-bit pixel fill with a Bresenham-style error accumulator: stores a fixed 16-bit value into a run of pixels, advancing to the next scanline via a byte row stride whenever the error term crosses zero; returns the fill value.

16-bit pixel fill with a per-pixel stride step plus a Bresenham-style conditional scanline advance: stores a fixed 16-bit value, steps the pointer by a small byte stride each pixel, and adds a larger row stride when the error accumulator crosses zero.

32-bit dword pixel fill with stride: writes constant dword a3 to a2 pixels starting at byte address 4*a1+a5, advancing 4*a4 bytes per write, returning a3; used by DrawRectangle (0x00553D70) to paint a scanline or row.

classes.name: TailJumpThunk
classes.responsibility: Forwarding thunks whose entire body is an unconditional tail jump (JUMPOUT) to a target address outside the packet, forwarding all declared __stdcall arguments unchanged without returning to the caller. Grouped by identical control shape; the real behavior lives at each target and the owning class is unknown.

classes.name: NullSubroutine
classes.responsibility: Empty no-op placeholder stubs: void bodies (some rendered as bare-return artifacts) that perform no work, touch no memory, and have no observable effect when called. Existence is inferred to be a referenced placeholder such as a callback, vtable slot, or deliberately disabled hook; no callers are recorded in the packet.

classes.name: FixedPointArithmetic
classes.responsibility: Small numeric primitives clustered at adjacent addresses: 16.16 fixed-point multiply with half-unit rounding, 16.16 fixed-point divide with sign re-application, and a truncating float-to-int conversion. The fixed-point scale is implied by the sibling multiply/divide pair, not independently stated in the packet.

classes.name: PixelFillPrimitives
classes.responsibility: Low-level pixel buffer routines: a 16-bit to 32-bit expanding blit with color-key skip, two 16-bit Bresenham-style pixel fills, and a 32-bit dword fill with stride used by DrawRectangle. Buffer layouts are flat base/stride/count parameters rather than surface structs.

classes.name: StringScanHelpers
classes.responsibility: Byte-level string/buffer scanning routines: a relative-offset strcpy-style copy and an n-th backslash locator. Both operate on flat byte buffers without class state.

compatibility_contracts.name: TailJumpThunkForwarding
compatibility_contracts.description: Each of the 20 JUMPOUT thunks must transfer control to its recorded target with the declared __stdcall arguments passed through unchanged and without returning to the caller. A replacement must preserve the target addresses (0x0051F8A1, 0x0051F991, 0x0051FB21, 0x0051FD31, 0x0051FEC1, 0x0051FF91, 0x00520051, 0x00520151, 0x00520211, 0x00520361, 0x00520431, 0x00520511, 0x005207D1, 0x00520881, 0x00520991, 0x00520A81, 0x00520C11, 0x00520E11, 0x005645B0) and the argument counts recorded per thunk.

compatibility_contracts.name: CrcChecksumCalculation
compatibility_contracts.description: Function 0x00527F21 computes a 32-bit checksum over a byte buffer: two 16-bit accumulators seeded from the seed argument, folded modulo 0xFFF1 in chunks of up to 5552 bytes, combined as (high << 16) | low; a null data pointer returns 1. The calling convention and prototype are only partially evidenced (legacy FAIL label, raw-source signature).

compatibility_contracts.name: NullSubroutineNoOp
compatibility_contracts.description: The 14 nullsub/placeholder stubs must remain callable no-ops: any caller reaching these addresses observes no state change, no memory access, and an immediate return. Their acceptance of various declared arguments (0 to 3) is not behaviorally significant.

compatibility_contracts.name: FixedPoint1616Semantics
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x00556790 must return the 16.16 fixed-point product of its two operands with half-unit rounding ((a1*a2 + 0x8000) >> 16); 0x005567A9 must return the fixed-point quotient with sign re-application ((abs(a1) << 16) / a2, sign restored). Any replacement arithmetic must preserve these exact rounding and sign behaviors.

compatibility_contracts.name: PixelFillAndBlitBufferContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Pixel routines operate on flat base/stride/count parameters: 0x005604C0 expands 16-bit source pixels into 32-bit destination dwords (two writes per source word) skipping the reference/color-key value; 0x00561970 and 0x005619AF fill 16-bit pixels with Bresenham error-accumulator scanline advance; 0x00561AF8 writes dword pixels with a byte stride and is used by DrawRectangle (0x00553D70). Exact surface semantics are unproven.

compatibility_contracts.name: MinHeapSiftDownLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x005385E0 maintains a binary min-heap whose owning object stores the count at +5190, a dword element array at +2898 (element index by 4 bytes), and per-element tie-break bytes at +5198; a parallel 16-bit key array is supplied by the caller. These offsets are read from the raw source and are not independently confirmed.

unresolved: The JUMPOUT targets of all 20 forwarding thunks (e.g. 0x0051F8A1 through 0x005645B0) are not recorded as callees in the packet; their identity, behavior, and the meaning of each thunk's forwarded arguments are unknown.

The owning class of every function in this packet is unknown; the five class groupings (TailJumpThunk, NullSubroutine, FixedPointArithmetic, PixelFillPrimitives, StringScanHelpers) are behavioral proposals, not confirmed source structure.
The min-heap object layout at 0x005385E0 (count at +5190, elements at +2898, tie-break at +5198) and the parallel key array layout are derived from the raw source only and are unconfirmed.

The CRC checksum 0x00527F21 carries a legacy FAIL ABI label with no prototype; the (seed, data, length) signature and the 0xFFF1 modulus semantics come from the raw source only, and the 'positive sp' style warnings elsewhere in the packet lower confidence in ABI details.

Functions 0x00554E04, 0x005631C4, and 0x0056498E are flagged by the decompiler with 'positive sp value has been detected' warnings; their bodies are unreliable and may reflect misdecoded data, fragments, or inline-asm artifacts rather than real routines.

0x0055685A (FNINIT then a1==0) and the MK_FP bare-return stubs 0x0052D294 / 0x0052D2A4 are probable Hex-Rays artifacts of inline-asm or bare-retn sequences; their true source shape is not recoverable from this packet.
0x005666AE forwards to sub_5666B0 which has no address or callee entry in the packet, so the delegation target's identity and semantics are unknown.

The pixel blit/fill routines (0x005604C0, 0x00561970, 0x005619AF, 0x00561AF8) use flat base/stride/count parameters; whether the 16-to-32-bit expansion double-write at 0x005604C0 targets one or two interleaved destination buffers is undetermined.
0x00540240 ReturnZero's caller sub_560FE0 expects a constant-zero result, but the reason and the caller's contract are not evidenced in the packet.

The empty stub placeholders (0x0052D214, 0x0052D224, 0x0052D294, 0x0052D2A4, 0x0053B590, 0x0053B5A0, 0x0053BB20, 0x0054632D, 0x00548DF4, 0x0054A574, 0x0055C7A6, 0x00563FFA, 0x005665A4, 0x005668EC) have no recorded callers, so whether they are vtable slots, callback placeholders, or disabled hooks cannot be determined.
The exact geometric primitives rendered by the Bresenham-style 16-bit fills (0x00561970, 0x005619AF) and the a3/a4 error-accumulator increment roles are inferred, not caller-confirmed.
